---
title: "Release data"
description: "Export working-stage tables from the GUI and create a complete schema-v4 portable project bundle programmatically."
---

## Two export levels

ProtVis currently provides two complementary export mechanisms.

### Release data GUI

The **Release data** page scans the current working directory for `.rda` stage files. Select one or more files, choose **xlsx** or **csv**, and click **Export**. ProtVis creates a folder per selected stage and exports data-frame-like objects; when a legacy/ProtVis project object is recognized it exports the expression matrix and aligned metadata.

This is convenient for quickly obtaining human-readable stage tables.

### Complete portable project export

For a reproducible schema-v4 release, use:

```r
export_dir <- export_protvis_dataset(
  dataset,
  directory = "ProtVis_release",
  include_raw = FALSE
)
```

This preserves much more than the GUI stage-table export. Depending on project content, the portable bundle can include:

- `ProtVis_dataset.rds`;
- active expression/sample/variable tables;
- annotations;
- process history;
- structured provenance;
- workflow status;
- result registry and immutable run records;
- generated artifacts/files;
- report/metadata outputs.

Set `include_raw = TRUE` only when copying source files is appropriate and licensing/privacy/storage constraints permit it.

## What to archive for a manuscript

Keep the exact quantitative input used for inference, sample metadata, statistical tables, enrichment backgrounds/results, figure source tables, search configuration/workflow, software/runtime versions, run registry/workflow status and the serialized project.

Do not use screenshots as the only copy of a scientific result.

::: {.callout-tip}
Record both **ProtVis 0.9.1** and the exact git commit used for the final analysis, because the `dev` branch is actively changing.
:::
